system_overview: This specification models a Multi Producer, Multi Consumer (MPMC) Disruptor, a high-performance inter-thread communication data structure based on the LMAX Exchange Disruptor pattern. Multiple producer threads publish events into a shared ring buffer, and multiple consumer threads read all published events in a multicast fashion (every consumer reads every event). The primary purpose of the model is to verify the absence of data races between producers and consumers and to check that all consumers eventually read all published values.
actors_and_components: The system consists of two types of participants: writers (producer threads) and readers (consumer threads). Writers compete to claim sequence numbers and publish events into slots of a fixed-size ring buffer. Readers independently track their progress and consume events from the ring buffer. The ring buffer itself is a shared circular data structure that tracks which slots are being read, which are being written, and the values stored in each slot.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the ring buffer contents, including the value stored in each slot, which readers are currently accessing each slot, and which writers are currently accessing each slot; (2) a shared counter representing the next sequence number available for a writer to claim; (3) the sequence number each writer has currently claimed; (4) for each slot in the ring buffer, whether it has been published in the current round (using an even/odd round encoding to distinguish successive writes to the same slot); (5) a read cursor per consumer indicating the last sequence number it has consumed; (6) a program counter per thread indicating whether it is currently accessing a slot or advancing to the next; (7) a history variable per consumer recording the sequence of all values that consumer has read, used for liveness verification.
initial_state: All ring buffer slots contain a null value with no active readers or writers. The next available sequence number is zero. All writers have a claimed sequence of negative one (indicating no claim). All publication flags are set to indicate unpublished. All read cursors start at negative one (no events consumed). All threads (both writers and readers) start in the advancing state. All consumer read histories are empty sequences.
actions: The system has four transitions: (1) Begin write: a writer claims the next available sequence number if the slowest consumer is far enough ahead that the writer will not overwrite unconsumed data (the consumer must be at most one full ring buffer cycle behind); the writer atomically increments the shared sequence counter, records its claimed sequence, writes its value into the corresponding ring buffer slot, marks itself as accessing that slot, and transitions to the accessing state. (2) End write: a writer that is currently accessing a slot finishes the write by removing itself from the slot's writer set, flipping the publication flag for that slot to indicate the new value is published, and transitioning back to the advancing state. (3) Begin read: a reader checks whether the next sequence number it needs to read has been published (using the even/odd round encoding); if so, it marks itself as accessing the corresponding slot, records the value read into its history, and transitions to the accessing state. (4) End read: a reader that is currently accessing a slot finishes the read by removing itself from the slot's reader set, advancing its read cursor, and transitioning back to the advancing state.
safety_properties: Two invariants must hold: (1) Type correctness: all variables remain within their expected domains. (2) No data races: for every slot in the ring buffer, no slot is simultaneously being read and written (the sets of active readers and active writers for each slot must not both be non-empty), and at most one writer accesses any given slot at a time.
liveness_properties: Eventually and permanently, every consumer must have read all published values in order. Specifically, for each consumer and each sequence number from zero up to the maximum, once that sequence number has been published it will eventually be the case that the consumer has read it and recorded the correct value.
model_bounds: The maximum number of published events bounds the model. The ring buffer has a fixed size. The sets of writers and readers are finite and specified as constants. A state constraint limits exploration to states where the next sequence number has not exceeded the maximum.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for consumer read actions (both beginning and ending reads), ensuring consumers make progress when enabled. No fairness is assumed for producers, meaning the model allows producers to stop publishing at any point. The publication mechanism uses an even/odd round encoding per slot: a producer flips the flag each time it publishes to a slot, and consumers check whether the flag matches the expected parity for the sequence number they want to read. The available published sequence for consumers is computed conservatively to handle the case where a slower producer has not yet published its slot even though a faster producer has published a later slot.
